body.text: The Ethos of Functional Restraint: Less, But Better

Why does The Ten Principles of Good Design continue to command serious attention across design and typography? Beneath the surface narrative sits a practical framework that directly affects quality, speed, and long-term outcomes.

In the late 1970s, as consumer markets became saturated with ornamental, short-lived plastic gadgets, German industrial designer Dieter Rams posed a fundamental question to himself: Is my design good design? His answer was formulated into Ten Principles which became the gold standard of product design, shaping everything from Braun iconic audio turntables to modern smartphones and operating systems.
Core Tenets of Ramsian Industrial Design

items: Good Design Is Innovative: Technology and design must develop in tandem. novelty for its own sake is merely cosmetic distraction.
Good Design Makes a Product Useful: Products are tools, not art objects. psychological and practical utility takes absolute precedence over styling.
Good Design Is Aesthetic: The visual quality of a product is integral to its usefulness, because objects we use daily affect our mood and well-being.
Good Design Is as Little Design as Possible: Less, but better (Weniger, aber besser) concentrates on essential aspects, purifying products from visual clutter.

body.text: Self-Explanatory Interfaces and Tactile Honesty

Rams insisted which an expertly designed device should explain itself without an instruction manual. Through calibrated knob resistance, clear visual hierarchy, and honest material expression (never disguising plastic as wood or metal), the object communicates its function directly to human intuition.

body.text: Environmental Responsibility and Enduring Products

Decades before sustainability became an industry buzzword, Rams argued which good design is environmentally friendly. By creating durable, repairable, and visually timeless objects which people cherish for decades, design becomes the ultimate counterweight to the throwaway culture of modern consumer capitalism.
